items.t: Adults: mild to moderate essential hypertension.

src.q: indicated in adults for the treatment of mild to moderate essential hypertension.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the UK lercanidipine 10 mg tablets SmPC.

items.t: Adults: 10 mg once daily at least 15 minutes before meals; may increase to 20 mg. Titrate gradually (maximum effect may take about 2 weeks). Higher doses are unlikely to help and side effects may increase.

src.q: The recommended dosage is 10 mg orally once a day at least 15 minutes before meals; the dose may be increased to 20 mg depending on the individual patient's response.
Dose titration should be gradual, because it may take about 2 weeks before the maximal antihypertensive effect is apparent.
it is unlikely that efficacy will be improved by higher doses; whereas side effects may increase.

items.t: Elderly: no dose adjustment needed, but take special care when starting.

src.q: special care should be exercised when initiating treatment in the elderly.

items.t: Safety and efficacy up to 18 years not established; no data.

src.q: the safety and efficacy of ZANIDIP in children aged up to 18 years have not been established. No data are available.

items.t: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction; untreated congestive cardiac failure; unstable angina; myocardial infarction within the past month.

src.q: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction. Untreated congestive cardiac failure. Unstable angina pectoris or recent (within 1 month) myocardial infarction.

items.t: Severe hepatic impairment; severe renal impairment (GFR <30 ml/min) including dialysis.

src.q: Severe hepatic impairment. Severe renal impairment (GFR < 30 ml/min), including patients undergoing dialysis

items.t: With strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, ciclosporin, or grapefruit/grapefruit juice.

src.q: Co-administration with: strong inhibitors of CYP3A4 (see section 4.5), ciclosporin (see section 4.5), grapefruit or grapefruit juice (see section 4.5).

items.t: Sick sinus syndrome without a pacemaker: caution. Left ventricular dysfunction: care required.

src.q: Lercanidipine should be administered with caution in patients with sick sinus syndrome (without a pacemaker).
care is required in patients with left ventricular dysfunction.

items.t: Ischaemic heart disease: caution; rarely angina may increase or MI occur.

src.q: Although lercanidipine is long-acting, caution is required in such patients.
Very rarely patients with pre-existing angina pectoris may experience increased frequency, duration or severity of these attacks.

items.t: Mild to moderate renal or hepatic impairment: special care when starting; increase to 20 mg with caution; consider dose adjustment in hepatic impairment.

src.q: Special care should be exercised when treatment is commenced in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment.
The antihypertensive effect may be enhanced in patients with moderate hepatic impairment and consequently an adjustment of the dosage should be considered.

items.t: Peritoneal dialysis: may cause cloudy effluent (raised triglycerides), which can be mistaken for infective peritonitis.

src.q: Lercanidipine has been associated with the development of cloudy peritoneal effluent in patients on peritoneal dialysis.
cloudy peritoneal effluent can be mistaken for infective peritonitis

items.t: Avoid alcohol (may potentiate effect). Galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption: should not take (contains lactose).

src.q: Alcohol should be avoided since it may potentiate the effect of vasodilating antihypertensive drugs
Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

items.t: CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, erythromycin, clarithromycin): large rise in lercanidipine levels (ketoconazole AUC 15-fold). Avoid; strong inhibitors are contraindicated.

src.q: Co-prescription of lercanidipine with inhibitors of CYP3A4 (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, erythromycin, troleandomycin, clarithromycin) should be avoided (see section 4.3).
a 15-fold increase of the AUC

items.t: Ciclosporin: levels of both rise; should not be given together. Grapefruit juice: should not be taken.

src.q: Ciclosporin and lercanidipine should not be administered together (see section 4.3).
Lercanidipine should not be taken with grapefruit or grapefruit juice (see section 4.3).

items.t: CYP3A4 inducers (phenytoin, phenobarbital, carbamazepine, rifampicin): concomitant use not recommended; if used, approach with caution and monitor blood pressure more often (effect may fall).

src.q: Concomitant use not recommended Inducers of CYP3A4

Co-administration of lercanidipine with CYP3A4 inducers like anticonvulsants (e.g. phenytoin, phenobarbital, carbamazepine) and rifampicin should be approached with caution since the antihypertensive effect may be reduced

items.t: Beta-blockers (e.g. metoprolol): lercanidipine bioavailability halved; can be used together but dose adjustment may be needed.

src.q: lercanidipine may be safely administered with β-adrenoceptor blocking drugs, but dose adjustment may be required.

items.t: Other blood pressure lowering medicines (e.g. alpha-blockers for urinary symptoms, tricyclic antidepressants, neuroleptics): increased hypotensive effect. Corticosteroids may reduce it.

src.q: an increased hypotensive effects may be observed when lercanidipine is administered with other medications affecting blood pressure, such as alphablockers for the treatment of urinary symptoms, tricyclic antidepressants, neuroleptics.
a reduction of the hypotensive effect may be observed with a concomitant use with corticosteroids.

items.t: Digoxin: monitor clinically for digoxin toxicity. Simvastatin: take lercanidipine in the morning and simvastatin in the evening (no interaction expected). Other CYP3A4 substrates (e.g. amiodarone, quinidine, sotalol): caution.

src.q: Patients on concomitant digoxin treatment should be closely monitored clinically for signs of digoxin toxicity.
No interaction is expected when lercanidipine is administered in the morning and simvastatin in the evening

items.t: Mild to moderate renal impairment: special care when starting; the 10 mg dose may be tolerated but increase to 20 mg with caution.

src.q: Special care should be exercised when treatment is commenced in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment. Although the usual recommended dose of 10 mg daily may be tolerated, an increase to 20 mg daily should be approached with caution.

items.t: SmPC: no human data; teratogenic effects seen with other dihydropyridines. Not recommended in pregnancy or in women of childbearing potential not using contraception.

items.t: BUMPS (calcium-channel blockers): no clear risks; calcium-channel blockers other than nifedipine are recommended only when benefits outweigh possible risks.

src.q: The other calcium channel blockers are less commonly used, and while not thought to cause problems, will only be recommended if the benefits of treating a potentially serious or lifestyle-impacting condition outweigh any possible risks.

items.t: SmPC: unknown if excreted in milk; risk to the infant cannot be excluded; should not be used during breastfeeding. (The SPS calcium-channel blocker breastfeeding page does not cover lercanidipine.)

items.t: Male fertility: reversible sperm changes reported with calcium-channel blockers; consider them as a cause if repeated IVF fails without other explanation.

src.q: the possibility of calcium channel blockers as the cause should be considered.

items.t: Most common reactions: peripheral oedema, headache, flushing, tachycardia, palpitations. Headache is listed as common.

src.q: The most commonly reported adverse reactions in clinical trials and in the post-marketing experience are: peripheral oedema, headache, flushing, tachycardia and palpitations.
Nervous system disorders Headache Dizziness Somnolence Syncope
